small_guidance:
- The GEMM is the dominant cost (M=1024, N=8192, K=8192). Expand the autotune space with larger K-tiles and 128×256 / 256×128 shapes (e.g. BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4) since the fixed 64×128×32 currently used is too small for K=8192.
- Add a GROUP_M block-swizzle (group size 8) in the GEMM kernel to improve L2 reuse across N tiles of a row group; this typically gives 10-20% on large K GEMMs.
- Drop the fixed BLOCK_N=128 constraint: store partials in a buffer sized by the autotuned BLOCK_N, or pre-pad N so any tile divides it, so the tuner is free to pick the best (M,N,K) tile without being shackled to a manual config.
large_guidance:
- Use a split-K / two-stage strategy where the GEMM kernel writes per-(m, k_block) partial max+sumexp directly (online softmax accumulator) instead of a full [M, NB] N-block buffer; this lets you choose BLOCK_N=N_tile freely and overlap the reduction with later K iterations. Alternatively, since LSE is a per-row scalar, a persistent kernel with one program per row-tile that streams all N columns in BLOCK_N chunks (accumulating an online LSE in registers) eliminates the second kernel entirely.
- Consider transposing W once at init (store W^T contiguous as [K, N]) so the inner B load is a coalesced row-major load instead of strided (stride_bn=K). Combined with vectorized 128-bit loads this can materially boost the K-loop throughput.
- Fuse the entire activation chain (two LeakyReLU collapse to one slope=1e-4, two GELUs) directly into the row-tile epilogue of the persistent GEMM-LSE kernel, removing the second launch and the Mx/Sx round-trip to HBM.
